title: SessionState
description: The state a view is welcomed with (welcome.state), as the host writes it.

join_url.description: What the TV's QR code points at. None when phones cannot reach the host.

language.description:
The language the visitors' screens speak now (#80): `en` or `sv`. The controller
switches it; a phone may keep its own.

sound.description:
Whether the table's layers may be heard (#282). The controller's sound switch turns it
off for the session; a new session starts with sound on.

ribbon.description:
The layer whose ribbon the table shows, chosen on the controller when more than one
open layer has ribbon panels (#231). None is Auto: the layer turned on last.

performance.description:
Whether the table and the controller show their frame meter (#262): frames per second,
the worst frame, and what each layer costs. Off when a session starts.

phones_paused.description: Whether the operator paused the phones (#335): they can look but not change the table.

tables.description:
How many views draw the table and run its layers now (#412). With none, no layer
publishes its live values and the controller says so.

recording.description: The recording running now (#522): the controller shows a red dot and its time.

RecordingInfo.description: What the controller shows while a recording runs: the red dot and the time (#522).

Chapter.description: A chapter mark: milliseconds since the start, and an optional title.

corners.description: Extent corners in WGS84 `[lon, lat]`: top left, top right, bottom right, bottom left.

calibration.description: The calibrated table view, when the site has a `calibration.json`.

data.description:
Datasets layers may read, by name, as site-relative paths served under `/site/`.
Holds the scene's `buildings` and `trees` and everything in the manifest's `data`.

tv.description: The site's TV dashboard settings (theme, pages), as written. Validated on the TV by `@mrstudio/dashboard`.

display.description: How the table's surfaces render (#134), as written: `quality` is `draft`, `good` or `best`.

palette.description: The table's palette (#93), as written. Surfaces resolve it against the SDK's sets.

mesh.description: The 3D model of the site (`scene.mesh`), for the editor to place it again.

SiteInfo.description: What surfaces need to know about the site.

rotation_deg.description: Bearing of the table's "up" edge, clockwise from north.
Compass bearing of the grid's "up" direction (towards row 0), clockwise from north.

Grid.description: The regular grid all engine data lives on. See `docs/contracts/engine.md`.

front.description:
The edge of the projected image where visitors stand. At-a-glance info goes there first,
because for a viewer at the front the model hides what is projected on the far side.

ribbons.description: What the projector's blank space around the model shows, per side (present.md, Ribbon).

glow.description: A soft glow in the projector's blank space in the model's own colours (#476, present.md, Ambient glow).

intro.description:
How the projected table opens when it starts and after the controller's Reset: the layers
fading in one after another (the default) or the zoom in from the city around it (#446).

TableSide.description: A side of the projected image.

Ribbon.description: One side's ribbon: `"off"`, `"auto"` (use the free band when there is one) or a size.

strength.description: 0 to 1: how bright the glow is at the model's edge.

Glow.description: The ambient glow around the model: the colours along the model's edges, or one colour for all of it.

oneOf.description: Each edge glows in the colours along it.
The whole margin glows in the model's dominant colour.
The layers at rest fade in one after another, bottom first, each part of a layer a moment after the one before.
The map starts zoomed out over the city around the table and slowly zooms in (#446).

style.description: A MapLibre style URL, or null for no basemap.

welcome.description: The line under the title on the controller's home screen, for visitors (#73).

languages.description:
The languages visitors can switch between (#80), the first the table starts in:
`["en", "sv"]`. Empty or one language: no switch.

translations.description:
The site's own words in other languages, by language and then by the English text:
`{ "sv": { "Sample district": "Exempelstadsdelen" } }`. Titles, the welcome line, button
names, slide titles and the like. A layer's own words are in its package (`locales/`).

zoom.description: Web map zoom (512 px tiles) at the window size the table was calibrated at.

bearing.description: Compass bearing of the window's "up", clockwise from north.

window.description: The window size the zoom belongs to. With it, the view survives a change of resolution.

TableCalibration.description: The map view the projector needs for the image to land on the physical model.

Palette.description:
The table's palette: one of the built-in sets the SDK knows (`night` when missing) and
the slots this table overrides, by slot name, as `#rrggbb`. Layers and custom layers
refer to slots (`@accent`, `@cat3`), so changing the palette recolours them all.

MeshInfo.description: `scene.mesh` as written, and whether the footprints are still raised beside it.

path.description: An STL (binary or ASCII), OBJ or GLB file.

up.description: Which of the file's axes points up. CAD and 3D printing use Z, glTF and many modelling tools Y.

mirror.description: Whether the model is a mirror image (its X axis is flipped), as some exports are.

offset.description:
A model in map coordinates (#344): this point of the file, in its own units with the
up axis made Z, is taken as its origin, so the numbers stay small. The anchor is where it lies.

anchor.description: Where the mesh's own origin (0, 0) is, after `offset`.

bearing_deg.description: Compass bearing of the mesh's +Y axis, clockwise from north. +X is 90 degrees clockwise from +Y.

base_m.description: Elevation of the mesh's z = 0, in the terrain's height datum.

ground_tolerance_m.description:
The mesh's ground never matches the terrain exactly. Cells where the mesh is less
than this above the terrain stay ground instead of becoming low obstacles.

oneOf.description: Y up, Z towards the viewer: read as (x, -z, y).

Up.description: The up axis of a mesh file.

layer.description: The layer package this instance runs.

intensity.description: How strongly the layer is drawn on the table, 0 to 2. 1 is as the layer intends.

button.description: How the site offers the layer on the controller. Empty fields fall back to the layer package.

hide.description: Ids of the controls the controller and phones leave out.

parent.description: For an item: the layer it belongs to. It has no button and comes on with that layer.

stack.description: For an item of a revealing layer (#606): 1 the surface stack, 2 (or none) the stack underneath.

steps.description: How Next moves through the layer, and a sequence's steps, as site.json has them.

step.description:
Where Next is, while the layer is on: a sequence's current step, or the sub-steps a
layer reported (`layer.substeps`).

shown_by.description: For the layer a sequence is showing as its current step: that sequence.

rest.description:
Part of the map at rest although its package is not a base or ambient layer: a layer
of the scene that site.json starts on and gives no button, such as a Map data layer
colouring the streets (#204). It has no button on the controller and stays on while
the button layers open and close.

selection.description: The entity picked on the table or the controller (#279): `{ set, id }`. Cleared when the layer goes off.

health.description:
Trouble the table reported while the layer is on (#259): it could not start or lost its
data, and is trying again. Absent while it runs as it should. Cleared when it goes off.

clock.description:
The layer's play head (#373), kept here so every view reads the same time. Absent until
the table sets one; cleared when the layer goes off.

icon.description: An icon name from the editor's set, such as `sun` or `route`.

group.description: The group of buttons it sits in on its rail, such as "Simulations".

order.description: Its place in the rail; lower first. Buttons without one follow the scene order.

hidden.description: Kept off the controller and phones without taking the layer out of the table (#58).

credit.description:
Who made what the layer shows, as one line under its name on the controller (#659),
such as "Artwork by Vishvi Rajakaruna and Fabio Latino".

legend.description: How the controller shows the layer's legend (#660). Without it, `auto`.

LayerButton.description:
The button that opens a layer on the controller: the words and icon the site's
author chose for it, and where on the controller it sits.

oneOf.description: Every row, in as many columns as it takes to fit the centre without scrolling.
Every row, one under the other.
Small swatches in columns, for a long legend.

LegendMode.description: How much of a layer's legend the controller shows (#660).

loop.description: After the last step, back to the first.

reveal.description: What Next does when a step's sub-steps (category reveals, staged builds) are done.

transition.description: How a sequence goes from one step to the next, unless a step says otherwise (#43).

sequence.description:
The steps of a sequence: other instances shown one after another. Only for layers
whose layer.json says `"sequence": true`, such as the slideshow.

Steps.description: How Next moves through a layer (`docs/contracts/present.md`, Steps).

oneOf.description: Next stops at the last sub-step; moving on needs Shift+Next (the Chalmers demo).
Next moves on to the next step after the last sub-step.

StepTransition.description:
How a sequence goes from one step to the next (#43). `Fade` cross-fades the two layers;
`Dip` fades the old one out to the empty map, then the new one in.

layer.description: The instance id this step shows.

params.description: Params the instance takes for this step only, such as another hour of the day.

duration_s.description: How long the step stays in timed mode.

next.description: Overrides the sequence's `reveal` for this step.

title.description: For the controller's info strip. The table never shows them.

notes.description:
What the guide says at this step (#98). Shown on the guide's phone and in the editor,
never on the table or the visitors' controller.

SequenceStep.description:
One step of a sequence. It shows another instance: a layer of the scene (which keeps its
own button) or one of the sequence's own items (which exist only inside it).

playing.description: Moving on by itself: timed mode, or sub-steps played one after another.

titles.description: For sub-steps: what each one is called, for the controller's legend.

StepState.description:
Where Next is in a layer (`docs/contracts/present.md`, Steps). For a sequence, `index`
and `count` count its steps and `sub` is the shown layer's sub-steps. For any other
layer they count its sub-steps: `index` is how many are revealed, 0 to `count`.

status.description:
`retrying`: it failed and starts again by itself in `retry_in` seconds. `failed`: it
failed and waits for Retry.

LayerHealth.description: A layer that is on but not running as it should (#259), as the table reported it.

LayerClock.description:
Where a layer's time is (#373): `value`, in the units of its `clock` time control, at the
host's moment `at` (milliseconds since 1970), moving `rate` units a second (0 when it stands
still). A view works out the time now from these, so the table sends a new one only when play
starts, stops, jumps or changes pace.

surface.description: The surface currently in the slot. It changes when the phone reconnects; the slot does not.

connected.description: False while the slot is held for a phone that dropped.

mood.description: One of `MOODS`: with the avatar, the fun name the pages show ("Sunny Fox").

name.description: The name the visitor gave themselves, instead of the fun name.
